A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VIP/PINN/VGI research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on continuous-time MPE, multi-agent MuJoCo, and a coupled oscillator, including value-gradient, activation-function, and loss ablations.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark and ablation results, including additional baseline comparisons and appendix experiments on dynamics noise and time-step sensitivity.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 and Algorithm 1 replace time-conditioned value/policy learning with a stationary formulation and remove terminal loss from the critic objective. Table 2 reduces network inputs, and dynamics/reward equations drop explicit time-interval conditioning. Although PINN and VGI remain central, the documented inputs and optimization procedure materially change.

E1.justification: The eight MPE/MuJoCo tasks and coupled oscillator are retained; Cheetah/HalfCheetah naming does not establish a new task. Appendix C.3 adds stochastic-dynamics variants of the two existing MPE tasks. The newly specified agent counts and state dimensionality clarify existing coverage rather than demonstrate additional benchmarks.

E2.justification: v3 adds HJBPPO to the MPE and MuJoCo comparisons in Figures 2 and 4; v1 only discussed it as related work. New Figure 9 evaluates MATD3, MAPPO, and MADDPG against VIP on four MuJoCo tasks. MADDPG previously participated only in the oscillator comparison.

E3.justification: Figure 6 drops the boundary-loss control, and Figure 7 substitutes anchor-weight variation for boundary-weight variation. Added protocols use Gaussian noise variances 0.1, 0.5, and 1.0 with average target distance, and a VIP-only oscillator sweep extending to Δt = 0.20. Existing simulator timing rules and Table 1 hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices C.3–C.4 test robustness to stochastic dynamics and failure under larger time steps, substantially expanding the investigation of applicability limits. Loss-removal and loss-weight analyses are revised for the terminal-loss-free method. Earlier gradient-surface and ReLU/Tanh analyses remain, with their appendix figures renumbered.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed mean benchmark curves, retain the seed range 111–120 in Table 1, and display graphical dispersion. v3 does not specify a changed run count, confidence-interval procedure, or significance test. Additional uncertainty-bearing plots accompany new results without establishing a different statistical practice.

E6.justification: Benchmark and loss-analysis results in Figures 2, 4, 6, and 7 change, alongside added comparator and robustness results. Revised Figure 6 shows a much larger penalty for removing anchor loss than v1. New appendix results show deterioration under stronger noise and large Δt. These are revised or additional findings, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 mixes an infinite-horizon value definition with finite-horizon HJB equations, terminal conditions, and proofs. v3 removes the time derivative and terminal boundary and revises the HJB and advantage derivations toward a stationary infinite-horizon formulation. Appendix A.5 also adds a time-invariance argument for a fixed contraction map; this changes the reasoning without resolving all justification gaps.

C1.justification: The central claims about PINN-based CT-MARL, VGI-enhanced value learning, and superior continuous-time benchmark performance remain. v3 explicitly qualifies its first contribution as addressing cooperative deterministic systems, making the claimed applicability more restricted and explicit.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limitations connecting noise sensitivity to absent diffusion/uncertainty modeling and large-step degradation to linearization and claimed contraction conditions. These qualify the earlier robustness narrative. The conclusion replaces v1's discussion of competitive-value discontinuities and state constraints with an HJI-based extension, while the anchor-loss explanation is adapted to absent terminal supervision.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code link, specifies coverage up to six agents and 113 state dimensions, and revises Table 2's network input dimensions. Hardware, hidden-layer architectures, learning rates, and other Table 1 settings remain documented as before. Some implementation prose still mentions time inputs despite the revised table.

R1.justification: v3 adds focused references and discussion on stochastic CTRL, PINN convergence, time-discretization robustness, and MATD3, while removing several broader citations. The central positioning around PINN-plus-VGI cooperative CT-MARL remains. HJBPPO's bibliographic update refers to the same work already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The introduction and VGI motivation are substantially rewritten, related-work discussion is reorganized, and methodology gains an explanatory roadmap and lemma introductions. Results discussion and the conclusion are reworked. Author-year citations, acknowledgments, an ethics statement, and an LLM-use disclosure further change the document's presentation.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 9, 12, and 13, redraws benchmark and loss-analysis displays with revised legends, axes, and categories, and adopts a conference layout with compact author information and running headers. Earlier appendix gradient and activation figures are retained as Figures 10–11, rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evaluation by adding the closely related HJBPPO and standard MARL comparators, while new noise and time-step tests expose failure regimes absent from v1. The stationary formulation also reduces the mismatch between the original value definition and HJB treatment. These address important weaknesses in validation and scope calibration. The theoretical cleanup remains incomplete: Appendix A.5 still does not establish contraction from bounded Jacobians and small Δt alone, and some input descriptions remain inconsistent.
